whatChanged.title: Share inside Technology rose from a low base
whatChanged.detail: Quantum coverage remained smaller than AI or semis, but its relative weight inside technology-general improved versus the prior quarter.

whatChanged.title: Evidence diversified beyond headline news
whatChanged.detail: Roadmap updates, public-sector funding language, and infrastructure narratives began appearing together instead of as isolated hardware headlines.

whyItMatters.summary: Quantum matters when it persists across research, policy, and commercialization evidence classes rather than flashing as a single-cycle media burst.
statements: A rising share from a small base is only meaningful if it repeats over multiple windows.
The theme becomes structurally more credible when error correction, platform roadmaps, and ecosystem tooling appear together.
This brief is a long-horizon monitoring object, not a buy or sell signal.

requiredClaims: Coverage growth should be visible in the quarterly aggregate and not be declining.
Subtopic movement should show quantum gaining or at least holding share inside technology-general.
At least one evidence lane beyond news should corroborate the theme.
provenanceExpectations: Use aggregate metrics for trend strength.
Use curated items or article clusters for narrative direction.
Use future filings, patents, or code activity as upgrade evidence.
notes: Do not treat general AI compute demand as quantum evidence.
Do not mark the theme as strong if only one vendor announcement dominates the quarter.

subtopicMovement.rationale: Roadmaps and processor announcements remain the visible edge of the theme.
Error-correction language is a stronger structural signal than raw qubit counts.
Tooling remains early, but recurring mentions would strengthen the commercialization case.

pathways.note: Roadmap and ecosystem evidence make IBM a recurring public-market reference point.
Pure-play exposure is useful for tracking narrative intensity, but not sufficient alone.
Small-cap specialists can amplify noise, so evidence burden should remain high.

risks.title: Narrative inflation from low absolute volume
risks.detail: A small lift in article count can look dramatic if the base is tiny.

risks.title: Vendor-led announcement concentration
risks.detail: If one company dominates the quarter, the theme may be over-read as structural progress.

watchpoints.trigger: More than one source class continues to confirm the theme
watchpoints.implication: Confidence rises that the quarter was not a one-cycle media spike.

watchpoints.trigger: Patents, public filings, or code activity appear alongside research and policy
watchpoints.implication: The theme graduates from curiosity to stronger commercialization monitoring.

prompts: What evidence would invalidate this quarter's rise as a structural change?
Which adjacent technology themes would quantum most likely borrow attention from next?

notes: The goal is section quality and evidence burden, not exact wording parity with generated output.
